name: dog
about: Chain ragdoll body for the feral dog (original-dog.glb, 25-joint rig). 13 capsules like the wolf: hips (root, pelvis to chest, the spine bone rides on it), chest (to the neck), head (neck to bite_tip; head, jaw, bite_tip and both ears ride on it), tail_a, tail_b, and 4 legs x (upper, lower). Bones without a body (root, spine, head, jaw, bite_tip, ear_L, ear_R, tail_3, the paws) follow their parent bone in the scene graph. Every number is here; src/chain.mjs holds none.
placeholder_note: radii, masses, joint limits and motor scales are PLACEHOLDERS to tune on Dom's phone and the clips; only the bone positions are measured.
scale_source: Armagedom Web/src/data/creatureDefinitions.json original-dog scale.model 2 (the actor wrapper's character 1.265 / visual 1.3225 multipliers are NOT applied here: the game applies them to the sim root): bones and radii below are in model units, the row is in metres at this scale (about 1.7 m long, 0.9 m at the ear tip)
mass_assumption: placeholder: a real feral dog is about 25 kg and 0.9 m long; this one is about 1.7 m long, so by volume several times that, but it is a 30 hp mob, so 87 kg total. The game data (health 30) gives no mass. Tune against how heavy the fall should feel.
inertia_source: data/ragdoll-role-table.json motor.inertia_multiplier (M1 finding), same value as the humanoid rows
hinge_flex_z_source: own, from the bone positions: the creature faces +z. Hind: hip z -0.23, shin (knee) z -0.12, paw z -0.248, so the knee points forward and the lower leg folds backward (-z). Front: hip z 0.11, shin z 0.09, paw z 0.16, so the elbow points backward and the lower leg folds forward (+z). Same convention as the wolf.

segments.source: placeholder: root, pelvis to chest (spine rides on it)
placeholder: neck to bite_tip (neck, head, jaw, bite_tip, ears as one capsule)
placeholder: tail_2 to tail_3 plus 0.04 model units past the last bone
placeholder: shin and paw as one capsule
